summary: Christian Lindtner (1949–2020) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his filosofiske doktorgrad from the University of Copenhagen in 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his Magister (1994) and Ph.D. (1998) from the University of Vienna, where he held a post in 1995. He later held posts at Stanford, UC Berkeley, and the Rubin Museum.

Christian Matthias Boehm works in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2005) under doctoral supervisor John T. Carpenter, having also studied under Toshifumi Konno.

Christian Parker Haskett is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, Michael Witzel, Michael Chamberlain, Lobsang Jamspal, and Geshe Lobsang Gyaltsen, earning a PhD from UW–Madison (attested 2010), and held a post at Washington and Lee.

Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields, having studied under Seizan Yanagida. He served as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008) and held a post at Hanazono University (attested 2011).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Stedelijk Gymnasium Haarlem and Leiden University (~1884–1888). He was an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and a professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She held a post as professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She held researcher and Director of Research posts at CNRS and was a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

Christmas Humphreys (1901–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1919–1922), and served as president of the Buddhist Society (~1924–1983).

Christoph Anderl (born 1963) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and linguistics. He earned an MA from the University of Vienna and a PhD from the University of Oslo under Christoph Harbsmeier, joining Ghent University as a permanent member around 2012.

Christoph Cüppers (born 1948) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1973–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, and Albrecht Wezler, later serving as director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1993–2013).

Christoph Emmrich (born 1965) specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels in 2004, holding posts at Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

Christoph Harbsmeier (born 1946) specializes in Sinology and linguistics, having studied at Merton College, Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D.). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia and the University of Oslo, and advisory professorships at Peking, Fudan, and Shanghai Normal Universities.

Christoph Kleine (born 1962) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his MA, PhD, and Habilitation at the University of Marburg, and held posts at EFEO, Hōbōgirin, Marburg, Munich (2004–2008), and Leipzig (2002–2005; 2008).

Christoph Theodosius Walther (1699–1741) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied theology at the University of Halle in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Tranquebar Mission from around 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf (1909–1995) studied under Leo Frobenius and at the University of Vienna and LSE. He held positions at the University of Vienna, Osmania University, and was Chair of Asian Anthropology at the University of London and SOAS.

Christophe Jaffrelot (born 1964) is a scholar of Indology who studied under Jean Leca at Sciences Po (~1987–1991). He held posts at Sciences Po (~1991), CNRS (~1991), and King's College London (~2012) as Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology.
Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who held a professorship at KU Leuven (attested 2009–2013) and an associate membership at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Christopher Byrne specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McGill University (attested 2015) for his PhD under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong, and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and Robin D. S. Yates.

Christopher D. Emms works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke (attested 2012–2026).
